answer: A thread enters ridge only by jury: incumbents drawn from the ridge certify one thread each per round, burning the ledge they staked. Rounds must be consecutive; a thread that misses one dies with its work. Because the pool is fixed, a thousand clones cannot queue in parallel — they compete for the same certifications, so each added thread burns extra ledge in the same round while the rounds do not shorten. The bill is ledge burned per certification, charged again every round, plus the work a failed thread loses. It breaks if the pool grows with headcount or certifications batch.
